not_examined.what: Concrete token implementations (fee-on-transfer, rebasing, ERC777 hooks, non-bool-returning tokens)
not_examined.why: No token implementations exist in the fixture; only the IERC20 interface. Effects are noted as assumptions where relevant.
Analysis was by reading the code by hand with worked numbers. Nothing was compiled or run, and no installs were allowed.

invariants.invariant: Every share burned in withdraw/redeem is worth at least the assets paid out: assetsOut <= shares * totalAssets / totalSupply
invariants.note: withdraw() rounds shares down (L36), so a caller can take assets while burning 0 shares whenever totalAssets > totalSupply.

invariants.invariant: A deposit of assets > 0 mints shares > 0, and existing holders' assets-per-share never drops because of someone else's deposit or withdraw
invariants.note: previewDeposit rounds down with no zero-share check (L23). A donation by the first depositor makes later deposits mint 0 shares.
deposit/withdraw/redeem update both by the same amount.

invariants.invariant: totalSupply > 0 implies totalAssets > 0 (no division by zero)
invariants.note: After assets are drained via the 0-share withdraw, totalSupply can stay > 0 while totalAssets == 0. deposit, withdraw and redeem then revert or pay nothing.

invariants.invariant: For each user, earned(a) counts only rewards accrued while a's stake was in place: userRewardPerTokenPaid[a] is checkpointed before staked[a] changes
invariants.note: stake() calls _updatePool() and not _updateUser() (L49), so new stake earns rewardPerToken accrued before it existed.

invariants.invariant: sum over users of earned(a) <= rewards emitted (rewardRate * elapsed while totalStaked > 0)
invariants.note: Broken as a result of the stake() checkpoint bug.

invariants.invariant: Emitted rewards are all distributable (no silent loss)
invariants.note: Low severity. Emissions while totalStaked == 0, and rounding-to-zero increments in rewardPerToken, are lost while lastUpdate still advances.

invariants.invariant: For every borrower, debtOf * 10000 <= collateralValue * LTV_BPS, using a price that cannot be manipulated
invariants.note: Checked only at borrow/withdraw time, against a spot price that anyone can move (public sync and donations) or replace outright (unauthenticated setPair). There is no liquidation path.

invariants.invariant: Only the owner can change risk parameters or the oracle
sum(collateralOf) <= collateral.balanceOf(pool); debt accounting matches transfers
invariants.note: Deposit, withdraw, borrow and repay change balances in step with the transfers. Over-repay reverts on underflow.

invariants.invariant: reserve0 * reserve1 does not decrease across swap0For1
invariants.note: Checked at L27 against the pre-swap reserves. No fee is charged. Rounding cannot favour the swapper because the check is an exact integer comparison.
sync() casts to uint112 without a bounds check (L18-19), so a balance above 2^112 is truncated silently. Practical only for tokens with very large supply.

invariants.invariant: sum of payouts <= balance, and each recipient gets floor(bal*share/10000)
invariants.note: The shares sum to 10000 (checked in the constructor). Rounding dust stays in the contract and is included in the next distribute(). No value is lost or redirected.

findings.title: ShareVault.withdraw rounds shares burned down: anyone can withdraw assets while burning 0 shares
findings.mechanism: shares = assets * totalSupply / totalAssets() uses floor division, which favours the withdrawer. When totalAssets > totalSupply (any yield or donation), any assets < totalAssets/totalSupply burns 0 shares. balanceOf[msg.sender] -= 0 succeeds even for an address holding no shares.
attack_sequence: State: totalSupply = 1 share and totalAssets = 1e18 + 1 (for example after the first-depositor donation, or simply a vault that has earned yield).
An attacker holding 0 shares calls withdraw(1e18): shares = 1e18 * 1 / (1e18 + 1) = 0.
balanceOf[attacker] -= 0 and totalSupply -= 0 both pass, and the vault transfers 1e18 to the attacker.

General case: with S shares and A assets, repeated calls to withdraw(ceil(A/S) - 1) drain A down to about S, taking all value above 1 asset per share. Example: S = 1000, A = 5000, withdraw(4) burns 0 shares; repeat.
preconditions: totalAssets > totalSupply, meaning the exchange rate is above 1. This follows from any yield or donation, and from the first-deposit scenario below.
findings.impact: Theft of vault assets by an account with no shares. In the worst case nearly the whole vault is drained. Honest holders' shares are left backed by about 1 wei each or less, and deposits can revert on division by zero once totalAssets reaches 0 while totalSupply > 0.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry test: alice deposits 1, then donates 1e18 directly to the vault. Bob (0 shares) calls withdraw(1e18). Assert that Bob received 1e18 and that totalSupply is unchanged. Fix by rounding up (mulDivUp) in withdraw and requiring shares > 0.

findings.title: ShareVault first-depositor share-inflation attack: later deposits mint 0 shares
findings.mechanism: On an empty vault, shares are minted 1:1. totalAssets() is the raw token balance, so a direct transfer raises the exchange rate. previewDeposit rounds down and deposit has no require(shares > 0), so a victim's deposit smaller than the share price mints 0 or few shares and the attacker captures the difference.
attack_sequence: The attacker deposits 1 wei into the empty vault and gets 1 share.
The attacker transfers 1e18 of the asset directly to the vault: totalAssets = 1e18 + 1, totalSupply = 1.
The victim deposits 1e18: shares = 1e18 * 1 / (1e18 + 1) = 0. The victim's 1e18 is taken and no shares are minted.
The attacker redeems 1 share: assets = 1 * (2e18 + 1) / 1, so the attacker takes the victim's deposit as well. (Alternatively, the withdraw rounding bug lets anyone take it.)
preconditions: The vault is empty or has a very small totalSupply. The attacker can front-run the first deposit or deposit first.
findings.impact: Theft of deposits made after the attacker's. A victim loses up to the full deposit. A partial version (losing up to about 1 share's worth, through rounding) applies to any deposit.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry test following the sequence above. Assert the victim's balanceOf is 0 and the attacker's redeem returns about 2e18. Mitigate with virtual shares/assets or a dead-share mint, plus require(shares > 0).

findings.title: RewardPool.stake does not checkpoint the user: new stake claims all historical rewardPerToken
findings.mechanism: stake() calls _updatePool() instead of _updateUser(msg.sender). Neither rewards[a] nor userRewardPerTokenPaid[a] is set before staked[a] grows. earned(a) = staked[a] * (rewardPerToken - userRewardPerTokenPaid[a]) then applies the full accumulated rewardPerToken to the new stake. For a fresh address userRewardPerTokenPaid = 0, so the stake is credited with every reward since deployment. An existing staker who tops up has the added amount credited back to their last checkpoint.
attack_sequence: State: rewardPerTokenStored = 5e18 (5 reward tokens accrued per staked token so far).
A fresh attacker stakes 1000 tokens. userRewardPerTokenPaid[attacker] stays 0.
In the same transaction or block the attacker calls claim(): earned = 1000 * (5e18 - 0) / 1e18 = 5000 reward tokens.

The attacker withdraws the 1000 stake. Net gain: 5000 reward tokens with essentially no time staked. This can be repeated from new addresses, or with a flash-loaned stake, until the reward balance is gone.
preconditions: rewardPerTokenStored > 0, meaning the pool has been running with stakers. The reward-token balance is enough to pay out.
findings.impact: Reward tokens are created out of thin air relative to emissions, and the reward reserve is drained. Honest stakers' claims then revert for lack of reward tokens, and rewards they earned are lost.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry test: alice stakes, warp 1000s with rate 1e18; bob (fresh) stakes 1000 and immediately calls claim. Assert that bob received about 1000 * rewardPerToken / 1e18 even though no time elapsed. Fix: call _updateUser(msg.sender) in stake().

findings.title: LendingPool.setPair is unauthenticated: anyone can swap in a fake price oracle and borrow everything
findings.mechanism: setPair lacks onlyOwner. price() reads getReserves() from whatever contract is stored in pair, so an attacker can set it to a contract returning (1, 2^112 - 1), or one that reverts.
attack_sequence: The attacker deploys FakePair with getReserves() returning (1, type(uint112).max).
The attacker calls setPair(FakePair). price is about 5.19e51.
The attacker deposits 1 wei of collateral, then calls borrow(debtToken.balanceOf(pool)). value = 1 * 5.19e51 / 1e18 is about 5.19e33, which is at least the debt, so the check passes.
Variant: setPair to a contract that reverts, so every borrow and withdrawCollateral reverts and all collateral is frozen.
findings.impact: Total loss of the pool's debtToken liquidity. An alternative griefing route freezes all collateral.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry test with a mock pair as described. Assert that the attacker drains debtToken. Fix: add onlyOwner to setPair (and preferably use a manipulation-resistant oracle).

findings.title: LendingPool prices collateral from manipulable SimplePair spot reserves (donate token1 + public sync)
findings.mechanism: price = reserve1 * 1e18 / reserve0 comes from instantaneous reserves. Anyone can raise reserve1 by sending token1 to the pair and calling the public sync(). The borrow check uses that price in the same transaction, and nothing ever re-checks the position (there is no liquidation).
attack_sequence: Pair r0 = 1000, r1 = 1000 (price 1). The attacker holds 10000 token0 and 9000 token1, and the pool holds at least 75000 token1.
The attacker deposits 10000 token0 as collateral (fair value 10000 token1, normal borrow limit 7500).
The attacker transfers 9000 token1 to the pair and calls sync(): r1 = 10000, price = 10.
The attacker borrows 75000 token1 (10000 * 10 * 0.75).
Optionally the attacker recovers part of the donation by sending 1000 token0 to the pair and calling swap0For1(5000) (k: 2000 * 5000 >= 1000 * 10000).
Net: spent about 10000 (collateral) + 9000 + 1000 (in token1 terms), received 75000 + 5000, profit about 60000. The position is far undercollateralised and is never repaid.
preconditions: Pair liquidity is shallow relative to the debtToken available in the pool and the attacker's collateral.
findings.impact: Bad debt and theft of lender funds up to the pool's debtToken balance.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry test with the numbers above. Assert that debtOf[attacker] is greater than the fair collateral value * 0.75 and that the attacker ends with a profit. Fix: use a TWAP or external oracle, and do not allow a donation followed by sync to set the price.

findings.title: LendingPool has no liquidation path, so debt can exceed collateral value permanently
findings.mechanism: The LTV invariant is enforced only when a borrower acts. After a price fall (r1/r0 drops, which anyone can cause with swap0For1), nobody has a function to seize collateral, and the borrower has no incentive to repay debt that exceeds the collateral's value.
attack_sequence: A borrower deposits 1000 token0 at price 1 and borrows 750.
The price falls to 0.5 (through swap0For1 or market moves). The collateral is now worth 500 against 750 of debt.
The rational borrower keeps the 750 and abandons the 1000 token0. The pool takes a loss of 250.
preconditions: The price moves against the collateral.
findings.impact: Bad debt builds up and lenders bear the losses. This is a design-level solvency failure.
findings.how_to_validate: Review the code: no function reduces another account's debtOf or collateralOf. Simulate the price drop and confirm that no actor can restore solvency.

findings.title: ShareVault deposit/withdraw division by zero once totalAssets reaches 0 with shares outstanding
findings.mechanism: previewDeposit and withdraw divide by totalAssets() whenever totalSupply > 0. If assets reach 0 (for example drained through the 0-share withdraw finding) while shares remain, deposits revert permanently and redeem pays 0.
attack_sequence: Drain the vault using the withdraw rounding bug until totalAssets == 0 and totalSupply > 0.
Every deposit() now reverts on division by zero, so the vault is bricked.
findings.impact: The vault is permanently unusable (follow-on effect of the rounding bug).
findings.how_to_validate: Continue the withdraw-rounding PoC until the balance is 0, then call deposit and expect a panic 0x12.

findings.title: RewardPool emissions lost during empty periods and through rounding-to-zero updates
findings.mechanism: When totalStaked == 0, rewardPerToken returns the stored value but _updatePool still moves lastUpdate forward, so those emissions are never assigned. When dt * rewardRate * 1e18 < totalStaked, the increment floors to 0 and lastUpdate still advances. Anyone can call stake(0) each block to keep throwing away accrual.
attack_sequence: rewardRate = 1 wei/s and totalStaked = 1e24.
A griefer calls stake(0) every 12 s: increment = 12 * 1 * 1e18 / 1e24 = 0, and lastUpdate is reset.
No rewards ever accrue to stakers, and the reward tokens stay stranded (there is no recovery function).
preconditions: A small rewardRate relative to totalStaked (for the griefing case), or periods with zero stakers.
findings.impact: Stakers lose rewards and reward tokens are stranded. No direct theft.
findings.how_to_validate: Foundry test: set the parameters above, call stake(0) every 12 s for N blocks, and assert that rewardPerTokenStored is unchanged.

findings.title: SimplePair swap input can be stolen between transfer and swap; uint112 truncation in sync
findings.mechanism: swap0For1 treats any token0 balance above reserve0 as the caller's input. If a user transfers token0 and calls swap in a separate transaction, anyone can call swap0For1 first and take the output, or call sync() to absorb the input. Separately, sync casts the balance to uint112 without checking, so a balance >= 2^112 truncates the reserve (for example 2^112 + 1 becomes 1), which would inflate LendingPool.price.
attack_sequence: The user sends 100 token0 to the pair (tx 1).
The attacker calls swap0For1(maxOut, attacker) before tx 2 and takes the token1 output.
preconditions: Non-atomic use (an EOA transfers and swaps in separate transactions). For truncation, a token supply above 2^112 units.
findings.impact: Loss of a user's swap input. Truncation is a theoretical lever for the oracle.
findings.how_to_validate: Unit test with two separate transactions, and a mock token with a large balance to observe the truncation.

findings.title: LendingPool.borrowers grows unboundedly with duplicates; borrowerCount miscounts
findings.mechanism: The push happens whenever debtOf == 0 before the borrow, including borrow(0) and every re-borrow after a full repay. The array is never pruned, so the count is inflated and the view loop's gas cost grows without bound.
attack_sequence: Call borrow(0) repeatedly from any address. Each call pushes a duplicate entry.
findings.impact: Off-chain monitoring gets wrong numbers, and borrowerCount() can eventually exceed the gas limit. No loss of funds.
findings.how_to_validate: Call borrow(0) 3 times and assert borrowerCount() == 3 even though there are no debtors.

notes: No findings for PayoutSplitter: floor rounding leaves dust that rolls into the next distribution, and payouts cannot exceed the balance because the shares sum to 10000. A token-hook re-entry into distribute() only causes a revert, and a blacklisting token could block distribution (liveness, depends on the token). No findings for SimplePair's k-invariant. No findings for the LendingPool rounding directions (price and value both floor, which favours the protocol). ShareVault.redeem rounds down, which correctly favours the vault. The issue is withdraw(). Assumptions: ShareVault and RewardPool credit the nominal amount before or after transferFrom, so fee-on-transfer tokens would over-credit; RewardPool never checks that it holds enough rewards. The PoCs were not run (analysis was by hand).
